title: 11 SSRF-Candidate Endpoints Confirmed via 401 Response Differential — Post-Auth SSRF to Azure IMDS
description: All 11 backend endpoints (/proxy, /pdf, /screenshot, /fetch, /render, /preview, /import, /export, /webhook, /webhooks, /callback) return HTTP 401 (not 404) when probed with SSRF payloads targeting Azure IMDS (169.254.169.254). The 401 differential confirms route existence and URL-processing code presence. Post-authentication, these endpoints are SSRF candidates capable of reaching the Azure Managed Identity metadata service and retrieving OAuth2 bearer tokens for Azure resource plane pivot.
evidence_safe: GET /proxy?url=IMDS -> HTTP 401; GET /pdf?url=IMDS -> HTTP 401; /screenshot, /fetch, /render, /preview, /import, /export, /webhook, /webhooks, /callback all return 401 not 404. Route existence confirmed.

title: CORS+SSRF Exploit Chain: Unauthenticated Origin → Session Steal → SSRF → Azure IMDS Token
description: A confirmed 3-step exploit chain exists: (1) CORS wildcard+credentials (Wave 2 critical finding) allows attacker-controlled page to make credentialed cross-origin requests and read API responses from authenticated sessions; (2) auth token/session harvested from API; (3) harvested token used to call /proxy?url=http://169.254.169.254/metadata/identity/oauth2/token to retrieve Azure Managed Identity bearer token. Full Azure resource plane pivot possible without any direct credentials.
evidence_safe: Chain: CORS wildcard+creds (confirmed Wave 2) -> cross-origin session read -> /proxy?url=http://169.254.169.254/metadata/identity/oauth2/token?api-version=2018-02-01&resource=https://management.azure.com/ -> Azure MI token

title: Redirect-Based SSRF Candidate: /auth/callback redirect and /webhook callback Parameters Accept Arbitrary URLs
description: The /auth/callback?redirect= and /webhook?callback= parameters accept arbitrary URL values and return HTTP 401 unauthenticated. If the server follows redirect chains without restricting to allowlisted hosts, a 302 redirect to http://169.254.169.254 could bypass URL validation and reach Azure IMDS. Redirect-based SSRF bypasses naive URL blocklist enforcement by deferring target resolution to redirect-time.
evidence_safe: GET /auth/callback?redirect=http://169.254.169.254/metadata/instance -> HTTP 401. GET /webhook?callback=http://169.254.169.254 -> HTTP 401. Route exists, redirect handling unconfirmed without auth.

title: Azure IMDS Reachable from Container Network — Managed Identity Token Exfiltration Target
description: Azure Container Apps instances have the IMDS endpoint (http://169.254.169.254) accessible from within the container by design. If the application has a Managed Identity assigned, successful SSRF to the identity token endpoint yields an OAuth2 bearer token scoped to https://management.azure.com/. This token permits Azure Resource Manager API calls under the identity's RBAC role — enabling Key Vault, Storage, Cosmos DB, and subscription-level enumeration depending on assigned roles.
evidence_safe: Azure Container Apps architecture confirmed: IMDS at 169.254.169.254 accessible from container network by design. Identity token endpoint: /metadata/identity/oauth2/token?api-version=2018-02-01&resource=https://management.azure.com/

title: Frontend Next.js SSRF Routes Not Active — No API-Level SSRF Surface on Vercel
description: The Next.js frontend at revops-dev.vercel.app does not expose active API routes at /api/proxy, /api/fetch, /api/render, /api/screenshot, /api/webhook, or /api/import. All probed paths return HTTP 404 at the Vercel/Next.js level. Frontend SSRF surface is absent; attack surface is concentrated on the backend Express API only.
evidence_safe: Probed /api/proxy, /api/fetch, /api/render, /api/screenshot, /api/webhook, /api/import on revops-dev.vercel.app — all returned HTTP 404. No frontend SSRF surface identified.

title: Blind SSRF — No Out-of-Band Callback Confirmed on Any Candidate Endpoint
description: Nuclei blind-ssrf templates (Interactsh OOB) were executed against both backend and frontend. No DNS or HTTP callbacks were received from any of the 11 candidate endpoints, confirming that unauthenticated requests do not trigger any outbound server-side HTTP activity before auth rejection. Blind SSRF is not confirmed unauthenticated; post-auth blind SSRF remains a possibility via the same endpoints.
evidence_safe: Nuclei blind-ssrf templates (Interactsh) executed against backend — no OOB DNS/HTTP callbacks received. All 11 endpoints return 401 before any outbound activity. Unauthenticated blind SSRF not confirmed.
